significance.justification: A verified-true result would license the specific form-(iii) predictive coupling that the "fraction of answer-position attention diverted to the distractor causally predicts per-example recall failure," together with the causal account that the fact "stays decodable in mid layers" and can be recovered by refocusing attention. This would establish both a behavioral phenomenon and a mechanism, constraining future explanations of these errors toward retrieval routing rather than erased or absent knowledge; Shi et al. (2023), "Large Language Models Can Be Easily Distracted by Irrelevant Context," documents the relevant behavioral degradation, while Geva et al. (2023), "Dissecting Recall of Factual Associations in Auto-Regressive Language Models," shows why identifying the affected retrieval pathway would matter mechanistically. True and false are distinguishable: a negative result would rule out answer-position distractor diversion as the general causal explanation, although it would leave other routing or ambiguity mechanisms open. The topic-substitution check lowers no credit here because deleting the claim-specific diversion–failure coupling, storage invariance, and causal repair leaves only the broad knowledge-retrieval topic, which would not merit this score.

reach.justification: The claim names two reusable handles: "DiversionScore = distractor mass / (subject + distractor mass)" as a diagnostic or predictor and a training-free "attention re-focusing" intervention that down-weights distractor-token key/value contributions. The score is available at the answer position and the intervention acts before the answer is emitted, so it offers limited ex-ante lead time rather than merely explaining an error afterward; however, practical uptake depends on identifying irrelevant spans and retrieval heads, making the immediate downstream users primarily model auditors and interpretability researchers. After per-model re-extraction, the qualitative diversion-to-failure coupling predicts what should recur, but the claim gives no architecture-invariant threshold or quantitative law and explicitly allows that effects "may be architecture-specific," limiting transfer beyond factual queries with identifiable distractors. The topic-substitution check supports an above-median score because the generic topic supplies neither this failure predictor nor the decode-time intervention; their usefulness comes from the claim-specific mechanism rather than from the importance of knowledge retrieval itself.
